history.heading: Kievan Rus' and Muscovy
paragraphs: The East Slavic state of Kievan Rus', founded in the 9th century with Kyiv as its capital, adopted Orthodox Christianity in 988 under Prince Vladimir. Russia, Ukraine and Belarus all trace their origins to it. The Mongol invasion of the 1230s–40s destroyed Kievan Rus', and Russian principalities paid tribute to the Golden Horde for over two centuries.
The Grand Duchy of Moscow rose to dominance and threw off Mongol rule in 1480. Ivan IV, "the Terrible", was crowned the first tsar in 1547 and began expansion into Siberia.

history.heading: The Russian Empire
paragraphs: After the Time of Troubles, the Romanov dynasty came to power in 1613. Peter the Great modernised Russia along Western lines and founded St. Petersburg as the new capital in 1703. Catherine the Great expanded the empire to the Black Sea. Russia defeated Napoleon's invasion in 1812.

The empire stretched from Eastern Europe to the Pacific. Serfdom was abolished in 1861. The 19th century saw a golden age of Russian literature and music, but also autocracy, revolutionary movements and defeat by Japan in 1905.

history.heading: The Soviet Union
paragraphs: The 1917 revolutions overthrew the tsar, and the Bolsheviks under Vladimir Lenin seized power. After a civil war, the Soviet Union was founded in 1922. Under Joseph Stalin, forced industrialisation, collectivisation, famine and the Great Terror killed millions.

The Soviet Union played a decisive role in defeating Nazi Germany in the Second World War, at the cost of around 27 million lives. It became a nuclear superpower, launched the first satellite (1957) and the first human into space, Yuri Gagarin (1961), and led the communist bloc in the Cold War. Mikhail Gorbachev's reforms in the late 1980s led to the Soviet Union's dissolution in 1991.

history.heading: The Russian Federation
paragraphs: Under Boris Yeltsin, the 1990s brought chaotic market reforms, economic collapse and wars in Chechnya. Vladimir Putin became president in 2000 and has dominated Russia since, restoring central control and becoming increasingly authoritarian.

Russia fought a war with Georgia in 2008, annexed Crimea in 2014 and backed separatists in eastern Ukraine. In February 2022 it launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the largest war in Europe since 1945, leading to sweeping Western sanctions.

culture.heading: Literature and music
paragraphs: Russian is the official language, and over 190 ethnic groups live in Russia, including Tatars, Bashkirs, Chechens and Chuvash, with many regional languages. The Russian Orthodox Church is the largest religion, and Islam is the second.

Russian writers Pushkin, Tolstoy, Dostoevsky, Chekhov, Pasternak and Solzhenitsyn, and composers Tchaikovsky, Rachmaninoff, Stravinsky and Shostakovich are among the most influential in history. The Bolshoi and Mariinsky ballets are world famous.

culture.heading: Traditions
paragraphs: Russian cuisine includes borscht, pelmeni (dumplings), blini, and caviar. Maslenitsa, a festival of pancakes, marks the end of winter. The Kremlin and Red Square in Moscow and the historic centre of St. Petersburg are UNESCO sites. Russia is strong in chess, ice hockey, figure skating and gymnastics.

politics.heading: Authoritarian state
paragraphs: Russia is formally a federal semi-presidential republic, but power is highly concentrated in the president. Constitutional changes in 2020 allowed Putin to remain in power until 2036. Opposition leader Alexei Navalny died in prison in 2024; independent media have been shut down, and criticism of the war is criminalised.

Russia is a permanent member of the UN Security Council and has the world's largest nuclear arsenal. It has close ties with China, Iran, North Korea and Belarus, and leads the Eurasian Economic Union and the CSTO. The International Criminal Court issued an arrest warrant for Putin in 2023.

economy.heading: Resources and war
paragraphs: Russia, the largest country in the world, has vast natural resources. It is one of the world's largest producers and exporters of oil, natural gas, coal, wheat, fertilisers, metals such as aluminium, nickel and palladium, and diamonds.

Since 2022 Western sanctions have cut Russia off from much of the global financial system and European energy markets; exports have shifted toward China, India and Türkiye. Military spending has boosted growth but caused labour shortages and high inflation. The currency is the ruble.
